newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israelis back Netanyahu following crackdown.
newsitem.headline: Israelis back Netanyahu following crackdown.

text.p: Most Israeli Jews are satisfied with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's steps following a Jerusalem suicide attack, an opinion poll published on Friday shows.

Netanyahu sealed off the West Bank and Gaza Strip and froze the handover of Palestinian customs duties after the July 30 market attack killed 16 people, including two bombers, and plunged peace talks deeper into crisis.

A Gallup poll of 510 Jewish adults for the daily Maariv showed 57 percent backed his handling of the situation, 39 percent were dissatisfied and four percent had no response. The poll had a 4.5 percent margin of error.
Israel has partly eased the "internal closure" between Palestinian towns inside the West Bank, retaining a ban preventing tens of thousands Palestinians workers from getting to their jobs in Israel.
Palestinians accused Israel on Thursday of imposing a "siege of starvation" on the Gaza Strip to punish them for the suicide bombings.
